text:
sam: Hey all — about to open a tiny PR to fix a noisy logger. Quick q: preferred branch naming and reviewers for a small infra-ish change?

maya: For branch names we use either `feature/TKT-1234-short-desc` or `fix/TKT-1234-short-desc` depending on scope. Prefer feature/ if behavior changes. Keep it <= 50 chars after the ticket.

sam: ok thanks. And merge strategy? squash or merge commit?

maya: squash for single-file or small bugfixes (<~10 files). For multi-component work keep it as a normal merge commit and link the rollout plan.

olivia: Also add a one-line summary in the PR body, then a short "before / after" and test steps. If it touches infra or CI, tag eng-infra and @nate.

sam: gotcha. I hit pre-commit locally and got this: 
```
black....................................................................Failed
isort...................................................................Failed
flake8..................................................................Passed
```

maya: run `pre-commit run --all-files` and `make fmt` in the repo root. Black + isort fixes should be auto-applyable. If something weird, `git add -A && git commit --amend --no-edit`.

nate: For reviewers: 1 code-owner + 1 optional maintainer. For CI/config changes we need at least one eng-infra approver. If you change Dockerfiles or deployment YAMLs, also add a changelog line.

sam: CI just fired, saw the bot: 

dev-bot: CI started for commit abc123 — https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/987 (tests running) :rocket:

sam: Who reviews small docs/README changes?

maya: Docs-only can be 1 quick reviewer from the team owning that doc, or if it's tiny you can ask for a single LGTM. Mark as "docs" in labels.

olivia: Quick PR checklist for FYI: 
- branch name with ticket
- short 1-line summary + before/after
- run `pre-commit` and unit tests locally
- add tests or explicit manual test steps
- tag code-owners and relevant team (@eng-runtime, @eng-infra, etc)
- add changelog entry if user-facing or infra-impacting
- keep PR < 500 LOC for faster reviews

sam: sweet — will follow that. Any special notes about branching strategy?

maya: main is protected. Use feature branches off main, rebase/squash locally rather than merging main into your branch. We prefer keeping history tidy.

nate: If you expect a longer-lived branch, keep it behind a draft PR and add automated merge labels. Also ping on #release-war-room if it affects release windows.

sam: perfect — pushing in 10, will ping for a quick pair review if you have time @maya :thumbsup:

maya: happy to pair for 10–15 to walk through the pre-commit fixes and small test run. Ping me when you're ready. :smile:
